relevance_note: Single case report of a boy with arterial tortuosity syndrome and a homozygous SLC2A10 variant: "revealed pathogenic variant: SLC2A10: NM_030777.4, c.685C>T (p.R229*) (p.Arg2297er) (Homozygote)".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; output assembled with a short Python script from hand-chosen values, spans checked verbatim by script. One in-scope person (label 'patient', single unnamed patient of a case report). The 'non-consanguineous unaffected parents' are neither tested nor affected and are given no rows. Contradictions/oddities in the paper: (1) the Abstract says 'hyper flexibility of the skin' but the Case presentation says 'no cutaneous or ocular involvement was observed'; both feature rows are emitted and the checklist item 'hyperextensible or lax skin (cutis laxa)' is set to not reported. (2) Echocardiography reports 'a normal main pulmonary artery' while CT angiography reports 'dilatation of the pulmonary trunk (16 mm)'; both rows emitted. (3) The protein change is printed twice, as 'p.R229*' and as 'p.Arg2297er' (apparently a typo); protein_hgvs_as_stated records 'p.R229*' and the second form is left uncorrected in the span. (4) The Abstract's Results/Conclusion contain unrelated text about stroke radiology services; ignored. 'Ultrasound of abdominal organs was normal' is a whole-investigation normal finding, recorded as written and excludes nothing more specific. Variant type not stated for this variant (only general 'loss-of-function mutations' about the gene), so not reported. Age at diagnosis taken as 'three-year-old' from 'a three-year-old boy who was referred ... but subsequently he was found to have ATS'. The general claim 'he exhibited all the characteristic features of this syndrome' was not used for any checklist item. Peripheral pulmonary artery stenosis was first 'suspicion' on echo, then stated as 'Pulmonary stenosis' on CT; recorded observed. Mesenteric artery tortuosity is mentioned only in the Discussion.
